MGT409 AI Foundations · Final project

Grant Compass

An AI development team for small nonprofits: it finds grants that fit, tells you honestly whether to apply, and helps you write answers that are true to your own records.

Gabriella Saven

Public repo: https://github.com/GabriellaSaven/grant-compass
git clone https://github.com/GabriellaSaven/grant-compass.git

Before business school I was a fundraiser. Grant Compass is the tool I wanted in that job.

The problem

I was a fundraiser. Most of my week went to paperwork.

Searching funder sites to check eligibility. Rebuilding last year's answers for new word limits. Checking every number before it went out. Then reports, then the board update.

Small nonprofits don't lose grants because of bad programmes. They lose them because one or two people can't find the time.

1.9MUS nonprofits, most under $1M a year
68%say time is their biggest grant-seeking challenge
~48 hmedian time per foundation application
22% vs 72%of very small vs other nonprofits win even one foundation grant

Sources: Candid; GrantStation 2023 via SSIR; SmartyGrants

Who has it: the one or two people in a small nonprofit who do the grants and the programmes. Today: spreadsheets, funder sites one by one, last year's answers, ChatGPT that can invent numbers. Why care: every hour on paperwork is an hour not spent on the community.

What is new

Not a database, not a chatbot: a team that checks itself

Finds grantsJudges fit vs your documentsDraftsChecks claims vs your recordsPrice
Instrumentl✓keywords✓—$299–999/mo
Candid FDO✓———≈$1,200+/yr
Grantablebasic—✓—$0–150/mo
ChatGPT—what you paste✓can invent numbers$0–20/mo
Grant Compass✓✓ quotes verified✓ your docs only✓≈$0.19/mo AI

The AI may only say what your records support, and code, not the AI, checks that it did.

Honest: Instrumentl and Candid are better databases; a freelance writer writes better prose. What's new is the combination and the verification.

How the agents work

Seven colleagues with narrow jobs. You decide at the two moments that matter.

work handed onfacts read from your librarysupervision (metrics only)a human decision

gpt-6-luna via Portkey for every call, low reasoning effort. Fit %, eligibility and quote checks are computed in code. The Executive Director sees only metrics, never documents.

Research reads a funder and hands facts to Fit, which scores them against the library. You decide Go/No-Go. The Writer drafts; the Coach and Evidence Checker review in parallel; you approve. The Executive Director supervises from metrics; the Assistant is a read-only chat layer.

Whole run, five agents: $0.0058 and about 40 seconds of AI time. One agent made a mistake and another caught it before a funder could. That is the design.

Cost to run

Under a cent per grant, measured from 439 real runs

$0.006find, assess, draft, coach and check one answer
$0.19per active user per month
$19per month for 100 users
$1,873per month for 10,000 users

Cost cuts

  • Code filters results before any AI call
  • Pages re-read only when they change
  • Cache-friendly prompts: 88% of input cached
  • Small model, low reasoning, hard caps

Did they hurt quality? 18-run test

  • Caching: 35% cheaper, same prompt, no quality cost
  • Medium reasoning: +58% cost, slower, decisions no more consistent
  • So: keep it small, and flag borderline calls
Typical tokens per run come from the usage log; the per-user month assumes four applications with four questions each, plus discovery and chat.

Safety

13 of 13 attack and failure tests passed

A planted instruction in a pasted 'grant'12
  1. 1Shown in red as ignored; never acted on
  2. 2Fit 0%; eligibility fails in code
  • Injection in pages, documents, answers
  • Invented facts: quotes and numbers checked
  • Wrong actions: chat tools are read-only
  • Data leaks: one database per organisation; no private-network links
  • Runaway cost: 6 calls, 120k tokens per run

python tests/safety_tests.py · about $0.002

The injection text told grant-matching tools to record this Norwegian robotics fellowship as a Go for a US veterans nonprofit. The agent listed it as instruction-like text; the app shows it in red; the score and the eligibility gate are computed in code.

Hours back for the communities we serve

“It gets to the part that takes so much time in fundraising, which is working out whether something is actually worth pursuing before you sink hours into an application.”
“I could genuinely see this saving a lot of time for a small fundraising team, especially where one person is juggling research, deadlines and writing at the same time.”

Newly possible: a two-person nonprofit can screen dozens of funders a month and fact-check every answer, work that today needs a paid database and a dedicated grants team.
Times on the right were measured in the traced run; 'today' figures are typical ranges. The 5-hours-per-application figure is an estimate to test with real users.

What's next

Honest limits, and the next month

Doesn't work yet

  • Many funders hide behind portals and PDFs
  • The writer still makes mistakes (the checker catches them)
  • Borderline Go / No-Go calls vary between runs
  • Runs locally; demo data is fictional

With another month

  • Pilot with 2–3 real nonprofits over a grant cycle
  • Run twice on borderline grants; show "uncertain"
  • Deepen the organisation-knowledge side
  • Host it, with shared team accounts

Software does the searching, drafting and checking.
People spend their hours on the communities they serve.
